title: Travel, problems & emergencies
goal: Handle problems while travelling — delays, lost things, theft, accidents — ask for help and talk about 'if … then'.
intro: Learn the words you hope never to need, and the very useful **conditional**: Odia can say 'if' with **ଯଦି … ତେବେ …**, or more compactly with a verb ending **-ଲେ**: ବର୍ଷା ହେଲେ 'if it rains'. You also meet the 'would' forms for imagined situations.

phrases.en: Where is the nearest police station?
How many hours late is the train?
The AC in my room isn't working.
Can you take me to this address?

grammar.title: 'If … then': ଯଦି … ତେବେ and the -ଲେ form
grammar.body:
**Full version**: **ଯଦି** + clause (present or past tense) + **ତେବେ** + result (usually future or a command): ଯଦି ବର୍ଷା ହୁଏ, ତେବେ ଆମେ ଯିବା ନାହିଁ.

**Everyday version**: replace the 'if' clause verb with the **-ଇଲେ / -ଲେ** form (it doesn't change for person) and drop ଯଦି and ତେବେ: ବର୍ଷା **ହେଲେ** 'if it rains', ତୁମେ ଡେରି **କଲେ** 'if you're late', ସମୟ **ଥିଲେ** 'if there's time'. Irregular verbs use their past stem: ଗଲେ, କଲେ, ଦେଲେ, ହେଲେ.

**Negative 'if not'**: put **ନ** before the -ଲେ form: ନ ଆସିଲେ 'if (you) don't come', ନହେଲେ 'otherwise'. The same -ଲେ form also means 'when (once)': ଘରେ ପହଞ୍ଚିଲେ ଫୋନ କରିବ 'phone when you get home'.

examples.native: ଯଦି ବର୍ଷା ହୁଏ, ତେବେ ଆମେ ଯିବା ନାହିଁ।
examples.roman: jôdi bôrsa hue, tebe ame jiba nahiṃ.
examples.en: If it rains, (then) we won't go.
If you're late, the train will leave.
If there's a problem, call me.

examples.native: ଟଙ୍କା ନ ଦେଲେ ଟିକଟ ମିଳିବ ନାହିଁ।
examples.roman: ṭôṅka nô dele ṭikôṭô miḷibô nahiṃ.
examples.en: If you don't pay, you won't get a ticket.

grammar.title: 'Would' and 'would have': imagined situations
grammar.body:
For things that aren't real, the 'if' clause uses **-ଇଥିଲେ** (had…) or **ଥିଲେ** (if there were), and the result clause uses the **conditional mood**:

**would do**: ମୁଁ କରନ୍ତି · ତୁମେ କରନ୍ତ · ସେ କରନ୍ତା · ଆପଣ / ସେମାନେ କରନ୍ତେ
**would have done**: ମୁଁ କରିଥାନ୍ତି · ତୁମେ କରିଥାନ୍ତ · ସେ କରିଥାନ୍ତା · ଆପଣ / ସେମାନେ କରିଥାନ୍ତେ
(ଆମେ / ତୁ: କରନ୍ତୁ, କରିଥାନ୍ତୁ.) Note that the ମୁଁ-form କରନ୍ତି looks like the ordinary respectful present କରନ୍ତି — the subject and the ‘if’ clause tell you which is meant.

These forms are common in everyday regrets and wishes: ଭଲ ହୋଇଥାନ୍ତା 'it would have been good'.

examples.native: ମୋ ପାଖରେ ସମୟ ଥିଲେ ମୁଁ ଆସନ୍ତି।
examples.roman: mo pakhôre sômôyô thile muṃ asônti.
examples.en: If I had time, I'd come.
If I had known, I'd have told you.
It would have been good if he/she had come.

examples.native: ତୁମେ ମୋ ଜାଗାରେ ଥିଲେ କ'ଣ କରନ୍ତ?
examples.roman: tume mo jagare thile kôṇô kôrôntô?
examples.en: What would you do in my place?

dialogue.title: A lost bag at the station
dialogue.setting: At Bhubaneswar railway station, Sam's bag has disappeared. He speaks to a railway police officer.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.en: Excuse me, my bag has gone missing!

lines.speaker: Officer
lines.en: Calm down. Where did you lose it?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ଏଇ ପ୍ଲାଟଫର୍ମରେ, ବେଞ୍ଚ ପାଖରେ। ମୁଁ ପାଣି କିଣିବାକୁ ଗଲି, ଫେରି ଦେଖିଲି ବ୍ୟାଗ ନାହିଁ।
lines.roman: ei plaṭphôrmôre, beñchô pakhôre. muṃ paṇi kiṇibaku gôli, pheri dekhili byagô nahiṃ.
lines.en: On this platform, by the bench. I went to buy water, came back and saw the bag was gone.

lines.speaker: Officer
lines.en: What's the bag like? What colour?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: କଳା ରଙ୍ଗର ଛୋଟ ବ୍ୟାଗ। ସେଥିରେ ମୋ ପାସପୋର୍ଟ ଅଛି।
lines.roman: kôḷa rôṅgôrô chhoṭô byagô. sethire mo pasporṭ ôchhi.
lines.en: A small black bag. My passport is in it.

lines.speaker: Officer
lines.native: ଚିନ୍ତା କରନ୍ତୁ ନାହିଁ। ଯଦି କେହି ପାଇଥିବେ, ତେବେ ଅଫିସରେ ଜମା କରିଥିବେ। ଚାଲନ୍ତୁ, ଦେଖିବା।
lines.roman: chinta kôrôntu nahiṃ. jôdi kehi paithibe, tebe ôphisôre jôma kôrithibe. chalôntu, dekhiba.
lines.en: Don't worry. If someone found it, they'll have handed it in at the office. Come, let's look.

lines.speaker: Officer
lines.native: ସବୁ ଜିନିଷ ଅଛି କି ନାହିଁ, ଦେଖିନିଅନ୍ତୁ।
lines.roman: sôbu jinisô ôchhi ki nahiṃ, dekhiniôntu.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.en: Everything's here. Thank you so much!

culture: India's single emergency number is **112** (ambulance **108**, women's helpline **181**). Railway stations have Railway Protection Force (RPF) and GRP police booths. People are generally quick to help a stranger in trouble — shouting **ବଞ୍ଚାଅ!** or simply 'help!' will draw a crowd. Keep a photocopy of your passport and visa separately, and save your hotel's address in Odia to show drivers.

tip.title: In an emergency
tip.body:
- Shout **ବଞ୍ଚାଅ!** 'Help!' and warn with **ସାବଧାନ!** 'Watch out!'
- Ask bystanders with the polite command: ପୋଲିସ **ଡାକନ୍ତୁ!** 'call the police!'
- India's emergency number is **112**; ambulance **108**.

sentences.en: Help! There's a fire!
Watch out, a car's coming!
Phone the police, quickly.
The ambulance is coming — don't worry.
Don't go there — it's dangerous.
Don't go near the fire.
Go carefully at night.
The police have arrived.
My phone was stolen on the bus.
The thief went that way.
Let's go to the police station.
I'm looking for my passport.
How much money was in your wallet?

sentences.native: ମୁଁ ଘରେ ଖୋଜିଲି, କିନ୍ତୁ ମିଳିଲା ନାହିଁ।
sentences.roman: muṃ ghôre khojili, kintu miḷila nahiṃ.
sentences.en: I searched at home, but didn't find it.
How far is the police station from here?
There's a lot of theft here — be careful.

tip.title: If: ଯଦି … ତେବେ, or just -ଲେ
tip.body:
- Full: **ଯଦି** + clause, **ତେବେ** + result: ଯଦି ସମସ୍ୟା ଅଛି, ତେବେ କୁହନ୍ତୁ.
- Everyday: put the 'if' verb in **-ଲେ** and drop ଯଦି/ତେବେ: ବର୍ଷା **ହେଲେ** 'if it rains', ତୁମେ ନ **ଆସିଲେ** 'if you don't come'.
- **ନହେଲେ** = otherwise, or else.

sentences.native: ଯଦି ତୁମେ ହଜିଯାଅ, ତେବେ ମୋତେ ଫୋନ କର।
sentences.roman: jôdi tume hôjijaô, tebe mote phonô kôrô.
sentences.en: If you get lost, call me.

sentences.native: ଜରୁରୀ ହେଲେ ମୋତେ ରାତିରେ ବି ଡାକନ୍ତୁ।
sentences.roman: jôruri hele mote ratire bi ḍakôntu.
sentences.en: If it's urgent, call me even at night.
Hurry up, or we'll miss the train.
If it rains, we'll stay home.

sentences.native: ତୁମେ ନ ଆସିଲେ ମୁଁ ଏକୁଟିଆ ଯିବି।
sentences.roman: tume nô asile muṃ ekuṭia jibi.
sentences.en: If you don't come, I'll go alone.

sentences.native: ଯଦି କିଛି ସମସ୍ୟା ଅଛି, ତେବେ କୁହନ୍ତୁ।
sentences.roman: jôdi kichhi sômôssya ôchhi, tebe kuhôntu.
sentences.en: If there's any problem, tell me.
Take an umbrella, or you'll get wet.
If you need money, tell me.
It's not urgent — we'll do it tomorrow.
The train will come two hours late.
Which platform will the Puri train come in on?
Today's bus has been cancelled.
All trains are cancelled because of the cyclone.
The train is running an hour late.

sentences.native: ଏହା ମୋ ସିଟ୍, ଆପଣଙ୍କ ସିଟ୍ ସେଠି।
sentences.roman: eha mo siṭ, apôṇôṅkô siṭ seṭhi.
sentences.en: This is my seat — yours is over there.
Is this seat free?
Is the shop open now?
No, it's closed on Sundays.
The window in my room is broken.
There's no water coming in the bathroom.
My phone has died.
What's the hotel's address?
Don't leave the door open.
The key's broken — the door won't open.

tip.title: Would and would have
tip.body:
- Imagined 'if': **ଥିଲେ** 'if there were', **-ଇଥିଲେ** 'if … had'.
- 'Would': ମୁଁ କିଣ**ନ୍ତି** · ଆପଣ ଡାକ**ନ୍ତେ** · ସେ ହୋଇ**ଥାନ୍ତା** ('would have').
- **ଭଲ ହୋଇଥାନ୍ତା** 'it would have been good' — a very common regret.

sentences.native: ବର୍ଷା ନ ହୋଇଥିଲେ ଆମେ ସମୁଦ୍ର କୂଳକୁ ଯାଇଥାନ୍ତୁ।
sentences.roman: bôrsa nô hoithile ame sômudrô kuḷôku jaithantu.
sentences.en: If it hadn't rained, we'd have gone to the beach.
It would have been better if he'd driven slowly.

sentences.native: ମୋ ପାଖରେ ଟଙ୍କା ଥିଲେ ମୁଁ ନୂଆ ଫୋନ କିଣନ୍ତି।
sentences.roman: mo pakhôre ṭôṅka thile muṃ nua phonô kiṇônti.
sentences.en: If I had the money, I'd buy a new phone.
If you'd come early, we'd have caught the train.

sentences.native: ଆପଣ ମୋ ଜାଗାରେ ଥିଲେ ପୋଲିସ ଡାକନ୍ତେ କି?
sentences.roman: apôṇô mo jagare thile polisô ḍakônte ki?
sentences.en: Would you call the police if you were me?

sentences.native: ସମୟ ଥିଲେ ମୁଁ ତୁମ ସହ ଯାଆନ୍ତି।
sentences.roman: sômôyô thile muṃ tumô sôhô jaônti.
sentences.en: If I had time, I'd go with you.
If he'd known, he'd have helped.
There's been an accident on the road — call an ambulance.
I left my things on the train!
Have you got all your things?
